failed_jobs_kept: eleven submissions are recorded, not one. Seven failed BEFORE any GPU work (a KeyError on a missing field, a template signature that had drifted from its call site, a missing brace) and one succeeded while VIOLATING the protocol -- it ran 25 launches per example instead of 40, which is what the device-time assertion caught. All are cheap because the preflight and the assertions are CPU-side, but the record matters: the protocol violation is the interesting one and it would have been invisible without criterion 2b.
note: The queue was empty before submission and no tenant was jumped. The job carried a 10m max-runtime. Superseded job 20260928t111322-e0720458 (25.05 ex/s, nvidia-smi sampling) by 20260928t112353-9a17d97c (168.81 ex/s, in-process NVML sampling). Both are kept: the first is the evidence for the 39 ms per-example sample cost that motivated the increment, and the second is the result of acting on it. The discriminator's own first two versions reported a confident H1 from a single run per mode, which the repeats showed was noise. Both are kept in job.json because a verdict retracted after three runs is part of the record, not something to quietly overwrite.
next_increment: queue_state() is now 94% of the remaining per-example cost (6.09 ms/call, it re-reads all ~500 job files per example). Fixing it touches a 6.6.6-owned module, so it belongs on its own bead.

restored_artifact.what: the discriminator's three diagnostic modes all wrote batch_summary.json, so the COMMITTED artifact of record ended up describing the slow reset diagnostic (7.54 ex/s) instead of the authoritative warm run -- and I committed that. A diagnostic that clobbers the thing it is diagnosing is the same class of defect as a stale artifact, wearing a FRESH timestamp, which is the most expensive version of it.

criterion_2_wired_into_criterion_7.what: the PI caught that criterion 7 asserted only that overhead falls and device time holds, so it PASSED on a run whose medians moved 15-25%. A throughput acceptance that certifies a run whose numbers changed is a speedometer, not an acceptance.
criterion_2_wired_into_criterion_7.fix: TestMediansReproduce is now inside the same suite as the speed guards, as an ordinary assertion rather than a note, so if the medians move the suite fails
criterion_2_wired_into_criterion_7.status: IT FAILS, and that failure is the bead's real status rather than a broken test. 14 tests: 13 pass, 1 fails, and the one that fails is criterion 2.

crashes_kept_because_each_one_looked_lik: Three of the four jobs above failed SILENTLY in a way that printed well-formed output: a NameError after the summary was built, a run that measured nothing and printed '0.00 ex/s', and a run that measured everything and wrote no artifact. A crash that looks like a measurement is more dangerous than one that looks like a crash, so all three are recorded rather than cleaned up.
